scope: Theorem 12.2 (Unequal marked intervals) of the manuscript “Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice” (preprints/Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2dda2109318f92bb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 95. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the physical tilted cylinder and horizontal-type marked bonds just defined. Its two cut intervals have m + 1 and n + 1 sites, with n ≥ m and M = m + n + 2 even. In each unmarked list the logarithmic site coordinates have imaginary parts −f and 1 − f, where 0 ≤ f ≤ 0.6. Their respective counts differ from m(1 − f), mf in the first unmarked list and from n(1 − f), nf in the second by at most a fixed constant. Let Hpoly be the sum of x|λ| over single unoriented polygons through the two specified bonds. Uniformly over these lists and their orders, for every ϵ > 0 there are Cϵ and mϵ such that Hpoly ≤ Cϵnϵ m−4/3 (n/m)1/3 (n ≥ m ≥ mϵ). Both Cϵ and mϵ may depend on the fixed bound for the count discrepancies.
